source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"A condition generally considered to carry fairly little relationship to the underlying structure or function of the lungs themselves in most cases","B":"A simple, isolated increase in the client's overall fluid intake, rather than the more complex mechanisms actually driving this particular condition","C":"Improved lung compliance and gas exchange, essentially the opposite of what this particular condition actually causes clinically in affected clients","D":"Diffuse inflammatory injury to the alveolar-capillary membrane, leading to increased permeability, fluid accumulation in the alveoli, and severe impairment of gas exchange"}}
source_row.rationale: ARDS results from diffuse inflammatory injury to the alveolar-capillary membrane (from various causes such as sepsis, trauma, or severe pneumonia), leading to increased permeability, fluid accumulation in the alveoli, and severe impairment of gas exchange, a life-threatening condition requiring intensive supportive care.
